messages.subject_clean: Nonparametric Bootstrap For Year-stratified N-mixture Model
messages.body_plain:
Hello group,

I have a question regarding the best way to implement a nonparametric bootstrap on a year-stratified N-mixture model. I am using a large dataset of point-counts that spans three years. Sites were generally surveyed twice in any given year. However, some sites were surveyed for two years, and others for only one (this is a subset of a larger point-count dataset, so for some sites, either the first year or second year of surveys are being excluded). In total, there are 876 unique points, and 1341 "sites" after stacking those that were surveyed for two years.

I was wondering how to set up a nonparametric bootstrap for a dataset with this much variability in number of years each site was surveyed? Does/can the example bootstrap outlined in section 2.3.4 of AHM v2 account for variability in number of years each site was surveyed?

And, a related question: should year always be included as a fixed effect on abundance in all models to help account for the breaking of the temporal structure and any "noise" that may introduce?

Thanks in advance for your help!

Best,
Tyler

messages.subject: UnmarkedFrameDSO nonparboot error
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am working on data collected during aerial survey, from 1997 to 2004.
First, I used UnmarkedFrameDSO function on my data and then use distsampOpen to add the effect of my variables which looks like that:
#-------------------------------
m4 <-
  distsampOpen(
    lambdaformula = ~vege + ele,
    gammaformula = ~year,
    omegaformula = ~year,
    pformula = ~ele,
    data = unm_Graz_apr,
    keyfun = "halfnorm",
    output = "abund",
    unitsOut = "kmsq",
    K= 100)
#------------------------------
Now, I would like to look at the estimation of the abundance each year and use bootstrapping to estimate the standard error. However, when I ran this:

npb <- nonparboot(m4, B=10) # I have an error
Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) :
  non-finite finite-difference value [4]

So, I tried to decrease B which was already very (too) small and it worked (B = 3). But then I have another error:

smoothed(npb)[2,]))
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘smoothed’ for signature ‘"unmarkedFitDSO"’

Same error if I do:
smoothed(m4)
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘smoothed’ for signature ‘"unmarkedFitDSO"’

Obviously, I am doing something wrong here but I can't figure it out what.
Thank you for your help.

Anne

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] UnmarkedFrameDSO nonparboot error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Anne,

If your dataset is relatively small (in terms of sites) and/or sparse, resampling the existing sites can easily result in new datasets which unmarked has problems fitting, especially considering this relatively complex model. So the higher the B the more chance you run into one of these and get an error. I believe it is possible to iteratively call nonparboot on the same model with small B to slowly build up working fits.

The smoothed function only works on dynamic occupancy models. Probably what you want for estimating abundance each year is ranef().

You may also consider fitting a "stacked" single-season model with year as a covariate if you have issues fitting the model, it's hard to get these dynamic abundance models to work.

Ken

messages.subject: GOF test for gdistremoval models
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am wondering what the best way is to assess Goodness of fit for models fit with gdistremoval.

The data structure: I have three seasons of point count data where I visited each site only once. I have 'stacked the years so that I have a total of 910 sites with only one visit. At each point I recorded both distance and time of detection which I binned and used for the yDistance and yRemoval arguments in my unmarkedFrameGDR. I have been able to run all my models but have trouble using the parboot function.

Before the gdistremoval function was released I was using gdistsamp and used the user-defined function:

fitstats <- function(fm) {
  observed <- getY(fm@data)
  expected <- fitted(fm)
  resids <- residuals(fm)
  sse <- sum(resids^2)
  chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
  freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
  out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
  return(out)
}

pb <- parboot(fm, fitstats, nsim=10, report=1)

This worked well for gdistsamp, but I realized I can't use this exact function this with gdistremoval because 1) getY(fm@data) returns only the yRemoval data and 2) fitted(fm) and residuals(fm) return a list of 2 matrices (one for dist and one for rem) that can not be squared or divided by etc.

I have tried manipulating the function a number of ways but have not had any luck getting it to work with parboot. Has anyone else found a good way to asses goodness of fit for gdistremoval models, either using parboot or other?

in case it helps, this is one example of what I tried:

fm<-<-gdistremoval(lambdaformula=~1, phiformula=~1, removalformula=~1, distanceformula=~1, BRSPumf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="abund", unitsOut="ha", mixture = "ZIP", engine = "TMB")

fitstats <- function(fm) {
  observed <- list(dist = fm@data@yDistance, rem = fm@data@yRemoval)
  observed<-cbind(observed$dist, observed$rem)
  expected <- fitted(fm)
  expected<-cbind(expected$dist, expected$rem)
  resids <- residuals(fm)
  resids<- cbind(resids$dist, resids$rem)
  sse <- sum(resids^2)
  chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
  freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
  out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
  return(out)
}

This works if you run it outside of parboot, but I get an error  when I run:
pb <- parboot(fm, fitstats, nsim=10, report=1)

Error in t.star[i, ] : subscript out of bounds

Thanks for any advice, sorry for the long email...

Katie

Here's a version that should work:

fitstats <- function(fm) {
  # Removal
  obs_rem <- fm@data@yRemoval
  exp_rem <- fitted(fm)$rem

  chisq_rem <- sum((obs_rem - exp_rem)^2 / exp_rem)
  sse_rem <- sum(residuals(fm)$rem^2)
  freetuke_rem <- sum((sqrt(obs_rem) - sqrt(exp_rem))^2)

  # Distance
  obs_dist <- fm@data@yDistance
  exp_dist <- fitted(fm)$dist

  chisq_dist <- sum((obs_dist - exp_dist)^2 / exp_dist)
  sse_dist <- sum(residuals(fm)$dist^2)
  freetuke_dist <- sum((sqrt(obs_dist) - sqrt(exp_dist))^2)

  c(SSE=sse_rem + sse_dist, Chisq = chisq_rem + chisq_dist,
    freemanTukey=freetuke_rem + freetuke_dist)
}

I'm not sure if this is actually a valid way to check the fit of this model considering the two separate detection components - maybe better to look at the stats for each detection model separately?

Ken

Marc

messages.subject: Extracting standard errors from occu()
messages.body_plain:
Happy holidays everyone,

I am running a series of simulations where I want to extract various outputs from a few thousand model runs. For example:

> out_test <- occu(formula = ~ bait ~ PC1, data = test)
> summary(out_test)

is working as expected and I'm able to access the AIC and parameter estimates as follows:

> out_test@AIC
> out_test@estimates@estimates$det      # table of estimates, SE, z, P|z| for detection
> out_test@estimates@estimates$state  # table ... for occupancy
> out_test@estimates@estimates$state@estimates   # mean estimates

However, I have not had any success accessing the standard errors, z values, or p-values associated with the @estimates tables. When I look at the structure of the tables there does not appear to be any slot where this information exist:

> str(out_test@estimates@estimates$state)
> showClass("unmarkedEstimate")

I suspect this has something to do with unmarked being an S4 class (?) but that is where my experience hits a brick wall. Is there a way to extract the standard errors, z values, and p-values from an unmarkedEstimate class object?

Best,
-ph

_________________
Philip DeWitt
Wildlife Ecologist
Ontario, Canada
